spots.name: Museum of Grenoble
spots.summary: The Museum of Grenoble is a municipal museum of Fine Arts and antiquities in the city of Grenoble in the Isère region of France.

spots.name: Perret tower
spots.summary: The Perret tower, originally called La tour pour regarder les montagnes, is an observation tower in Grenoble, in the Paul Mistral public park. It was the first tower built of reinforced concrete in Europe. In 1998 it was officially declared a national heritage site.

spots.name: Grenoble Cathedral
spots.summary: Grenoble Cathedral is a Roman Catholic church located in the town of Grenoble, France. It is a national monument, and is the seat of the Bishop of Grenoble.

spots.name: Bastille
spots.summary: The Bastille is a fortress culminating at 476 m (1,561ft) above sea level, located at the south end of the Chartreuse mountain range and overlooking the city of Grenoble, France. The Bastille, which also gives its name to the hill, is the main tourist site of the Grenoble area, with 600,000 visitors per year.

spots.summary: The Collegiate Church of Saint-André, Grenoble is a parish church, formerly a collegiate church, dedicated to Saint Andrew, in Grenoble, France.

spots.name: Grenoble Archaeological Museum
spots.summary: Grenoble Archaeological Museum is a museum located in Grenoble, France. It occupies the historic site of Saint-Laurent at the foot of the Bastille on the right bank of the Isère.

spots.name: Lycée Champollion
spots.summary: The lycée Champollion or "Champo" is a French secondary school and higher education establishment in Grenoble, at 1 Cours Lafontaine, one block from the Place Victor Hugo. Its present director is M. Neves. It was M. Mattone before him.

spots.name: Musée de l'Ancien Évêché
spots.summary: The Musée de l'Ancien Évêché is a departmental museum located in Grenoble, France and dedicated to the Isère heritage through the history of its Bishop's palace. Inaugurated in 1998, it is settled in the former Bishop's palace, near Grenoble Cathedral.

spots.name: Néron
spots.summary: The Néron is a mountain in the French department of Isère at 1,299 metres in the Chartreuse massif in the Alps.

spots.summary: The Couvent des Minimes de Grenoble is a former monastery constructed about 1644 by the Minim friars, a semi-contemplative mendicant order, which is located on the Rue du Vieux Temple in Grenoble, France.

spots.summary: La Casamaures is a historic 19th century villa, in the commune of Saint-Martin-le-Vinoux near Grenoble, in the Department of Isère, within the Auvergne-Rhône-Alpes region of France. A listed French Monument historique, it is undergoing restoration.

spots.name: Musée dauphinois
spots.summary: The Musée dauphinois, located in Grenoble (France), is dedicated to the ethnography, archaeology, history and society of the former province of Dauphiné, encompassing the current departments of Isère, Drôme, and Hautes-Alpes.

spots.name: Natural History Museum, Grenoble
spots.summary: The Natural History Museum of Grenoble is a municipal museum founded in 1851, in Grenoble, France. Since the opening of the building in 1855, it has showcased a rich natural heritage, in particular, alpine heritage.

spots.summary: Cularo was the name of the Gallic city which evolved into modern Grenoble. It was renamed Gratianopolis in 381 to honor Roman emperor Gratian.

spots.name: Hôtel de Ville, Grenoble
spots.summary: The Hôtel de Ville is the local seat of government in Grenoble, France. It was designated a monument historique by the French government in 2023.

spots.name: Le Magasin
spots.summary: Founded in 1986, Le Magasin – Centre National d'Art Contemporain is housed in an industrial hall, built for the 1900 Paris World's Fair by the workshops of Gustave Eiffel.

spots.name: Lycée Stendhal
spots.summary: The lycée Stendhal, formerly Cité scolaire Stendhal, is a secondary and higher education establishment in Grenoble. It is the oldest lycée in Grenoble, and its pupils have included Stendhal and Champollion. It is located at 1 bis, place Jean-Achard.

spots.name: Institut Néel
spots.summary: Institut Néel is a research laboratory in condensed matter physics located on Polygone Scientifique in Grenoble, France. It is named after scientist Louis Néel.

spots.name: Parc Paul Mistral
spots.summary: A big park in the centre of the city. It includes a roller skating rink and people often play street hockey. The park also boasts extensive lawns and quiet tree-lined avenues. At the centre stands the tower Perret, built in 1925 for an international exposition about water-power.
